The request went away before it was answered: its page closed, or the
plugin was turned off.

An `https` address to open in the client's browser, from a click in
the plugin's page. The client holds it to its reach rule like any
other address.

Profile.description:
A saved launch composition. `overlays` are composed into the session so
their skills and agents resolve; `access` is which folders the session
may touch. The two are not the same thing.

access.description: Folders the session may also touch.

openingPrompt.description: Submitted as the session's first message.

overlays.description: Project paths composed into the session as plugins.

root.description: The folder the session runs in.

ProfileDocument.description:
A profile as a portable document: what `profile:export` returns and
`profile:import` takes.

fileName.description:
From export, the file name to suggest; on import, the name of the file
it was read from, so an error can name it.

ProfileDraft.description: A profile before the host has given it an identity.

harnessPath.description: The harness this project belongs to, if any.

path.description: Absolute and normalised; a project's identity across scans.

ProjectKind.description: What a discovered folder turned out to be.

oneOf.description: Has a `harness.yaml`. Its `repos/*` children are projects too.
A repository inside a harness's `repos/`.
Neither, scanned because a root pointed at it.

path.description: The folder the shell starts in.

separate.description: A shell of its own, for a terminal tab, rather than the folder's one.

shell.description:
The executable to run. Null means the terminal-shell setting, and
failing that whatever the host detects.

problem.description: A sentence about what went wrong, or null.

requested.description: What was asked for when that is not what runs; null when they agree.

PtermStreamOpen.description: Which plain terminal a `pterm:data` stream carries.

Refused.description: The host's answer to a `hello` it cannot accept. Frozen across majors.

message.description: A sentence naming both versions and which side to update.

path.description: The addressed file: a skill's `SKILL.md`, not its folder.

frontmatterRenamed.description: The moved file's frontmatter `name:` was updated to match.

path.description: The addressed file at its new place, or null when nothing moved.

RenameHistorySessionRequest.description:
Naming a conversation in history. Null, or only whitespace, restores the
title derived from its prompts.

RenameSessionRequest.description:
Renaming a session's tab. Null, or only whitespace, clears the label and
the tab reads the session's name again.

RenderedCode.description: Highlighted source, for a config file a session runs.

highlighted.description:
False when there is no grammar for it, which is not the same as
highlighted as plain text.

endLine.description: The line the closing fence sits on, 1-based.

error.description: Set when the block is not parseable YAML.

present.description: A file with no `---` block has none.

html.description: Sanitised HTML. A client injects it and never evaluates it.

unknownLanguages.description: Languages a code fence asked for that had no grammar.

Request.description: A call on a request channel.

id.description: Chosen by the client, unique among its requests in flight.

RestorableSession.description:
A session the host's last run was hosting when it stopped without shutting
down.

blocked.description: Why it cannot be reopened, as a sentence, or null when it can.

lastAt.description: When it was last spoken to, epoch ms, or null when not known.

profile.description: The profile it was launched from, by name, or null for none.

profileGone.description: True when its profile has since been deleted. It reopens without.

RestoreOffer.description:
What a crash took, offered back once. Where each session goes on screen is
the client's: the layout belongs to the device, not the host.

elsewhere.description:
How many more were lost whose conversation is still running elsewhere.
Left alone: reopening one would be a second process on one
conversation.

sessions.description: In the order their tabs were in.

RestoreSnapshotRequest.description: Puts a snapshot's bytes back at `path`.

from.description: The lost row the session reopened.

ResumeSessionRequest.description:
Reopening a conversation: an id and a grid. The folder and the command are
decided by the host from its own index.

history.description: The history row it came from.

created.description: What landed, relative to the template.

id.description: Null to create; an id to update that profile in place.

problems.description: Field-level problems. Non-empty means nothing was written.

includeGit.description:
Read git state during the scan. A first paint skips it and refreshes
after.

error.description: Set when the last scan failed outright rather than returning errors.

ScopedFile.description: One file in a scope: whose versions to list, or which file to open.

SecretInfo.description: A stored secret, without its value.

hosts.description: Canonical origins the value may be sent to.

plugins.description: Plugin ids that may use it.

value.description:
Null keeps the stored value: changing who may use a secret is not
typing it again.

available.description: Whether the host can encrypt. When it cannot, nothing can be stored.

SessionActivity.description: What a live session says it is doing, in its backend's own records.

SessionActivityState.description:
What one hosted session is doing. Null activity is ordinary: no record
yet, a process not proved alive, or a status the host does not know.

conversationId.description:
The conversation id the agent reports now. Not necessarily the
record's: a cleared conversation gets a new one in the same process.

waitingFor.description: The agent's own sentence for a `waiting` session. Null otherwise.

SessionConfirmRequest.description:
"This session is still running": asked by the host, answered by a client
on `session:confirmed`.

id.description: Correlates the answer with the question.

sessionNames.description: Names of the sessions this ends, for the dialog to list.

ids.description: The sessions on screen: the front tab of each pane showing one.

SessionPort.description: A listening socket held somewhere in a session's process tree.

addresses.description: Every local address it is bound to, sorted.

process.description: The image name of the process holding it.

SessionProcess.description: One process in a hosted session's tree.

commandLine.description: The full command line, or null where the OS would not give it up.

depth.description: How far below the session's own process this sits. The root is 0.

ports.description:
Listening ports, ascending, or null where the socket query could not
run. Never merged with `[]`.

SessionRecord.description: One hosted agent process, from spawn to exit.

argv.description: Arguments after the executable, as spawned.

backend.description: The agent backend running it. Claude Code is `claude-code`.

branch.description:
The branch `cwd` was on when this was spawned. Null for a folder that
is not a repository, a detached HEAD, or a read that failed.

conversationId.description:
The agent's own id for the conversation this session is having, or
null. Assigned at launch where the backend lets Floti pick it (Claude
Code's `--session-id`); a resumed session carries the id it resumed.

endedAt.description: ISO 8601, or null while running and for a lost session.

exitCode.description:
Null while running, and for a session whose exit code was never
observed.

label.description: What Floti calls it on screen, or null for "use `name`".

name.description:
The name handed to the agent, so the session can be found in its own
resume list later. Never rewritten; a rename writes `label`.

profileId.description:
The profile it was launched from, if it was one. The session outlives
a deleted profile.

projectPath.description: The discovered project it was launched against, if it was one.

SessionResources.description:
What one hosted session is holding. "Could not look" is null and "nothing
there" is empty, and the two are never merged.

atMs.description: When the pass ran, epoch ms.

opaque.description: How many processes in the tree would not give up a command line.

processes.description: The tree under `rootPid`, root first then breadth-first, or null.

rootPid.description: The terminal's pid: the root of the tree.

SessionStatus.description:
How a hosted session ended, or that it has not.

`lost` is a row that was still `running` when the process that owned it
went away: a crash, a kill, a power cut. Stamping an end time later would
invent a duration nobody measured.

SessionStreamOpen.description: Which session's terminal a `session:data` stream carries.

SessionToRestore.description: One lost session to reopen, at the grid of the pane it goes back to.

readAtMs.description: When the records were read, epoch ms.

sessions.description: Hosted first, then the rest; each group by start time, newest last.

watching.description: False means this client is not looking any more.

SettingCandidate.description: One layer's value for a setting.

error.description: Set when the file is there but could not be parsed.

SetupStatus.description: What setup found for each agent backend the host can run.

SharedName.description: A name carried by more than one source, each under its own invocation.

Snapshot.description:
The whole current state of a channel that carries state, sent first on
every subscription.

seq.description:
The number of the last event this state includes. The next event is
`seq + 1`.

SourceToRender.description:
Text to render or highlight as the file at `path` would be. The text is
what is in the editor, which may not be on disk.

StartSessionRequest.description:
A new session with everything it is launched with, short of Floti's
agent tools, which the host registers for each launch itself.

The composition starts from the saved profile `profile_id` names, or from
nothing. Each composition field that is set replaces the profile's; a null
one keeps it. The folder is always `cwd`, never the profile's root.

agent.description: A named agent definition to run as.

backend.description: The agent backend to run, or null for the host's default.

cols.description: Initial grid, from the pane that will host it.

cwd.description: The folder the session runs in.

extraFolders.description: Further folders the session may work in: a profile's access.

name.description: Basis for the session's name, made unique against running sessions.

openingPrompt.description: Submitted as the session's first message.

overlays.description: Project paths composed into the session as overlays.

profileId.description: The saved profile whose composition the session starts from, or null.

projectPath.description:
The discovered project this is, when it is one. Recorded, not used to
launch.

reason.description: Why, when it did not end normally.

StreamCredit.description: More credit from a stream's receiver: the sender may send `bytes` more.

StreamData.description: Bytes on a stream, never more than the receiver's credit allows.

StreamOpen.description:
Open a byte stream on a stream channel. Each direction starts with
`DEFAULT_INITIAL_CREDIT` bytes of credit.

params.description: What to open, typed by the channel.

stream.description: Chosen by the side that opens it.

subscription.description: Chosen by the client; every snapshot and event for it carries it.

SubscriptionError.description:
A subscription the host did not start, and why. Nothing is ever sent for
it; the client may subscribe again under the same number.

channel.description: The channel the subscription named, as it named it.

TemplateChoice.description: One row of the template picker.

builtIn.description: The built-in scaffold, which has no folder behind it.

id.description:
The folder name, and what a harness records. `minimal` for the
built-in scaffold.

template.description: The template that is gone, or null when nothing was removed.

hasManifest.description: Whether there is a `template.yaml` at all; absent is legal.

modifiedAtMs.description: The newest modification time in the tree.

TemplateFile.description: One file in a template, and what a harness would receive it as.

link.description: A link, which is refused. Listed so the author can see why.

relPath.description: Relative to the template folder, forward-slashed.

substituted.description: A `.tpl`, whose placeholders are filled in on the way out.

target.description: The path a new harness gets; empty when the file is not written.

created.description: Targets that did not exist before, relative to the template.

replaced.description: Targets that did, and were replaced.

problems.description: One sentence per template that could not be read.

TemplatePreview.description: What a new harness's "What gets written" lists.

entries.description: The manifest first, then everything else by path.

template.description: The template's id afterwards, or null when nothing was written.

TestedRange.description: The versions of a backend this host was tested against, inclusive.

reason.description: Why it could not be reopened, as a sentence.

UpdateSide.description: Which side has to be updated for two versions to talk.

UsageGroup.description: The two windows a limit is measured over.

UsageLimit.description: One plan limit, after every field has been checked.

isActive.description: Whether this is the limit currently binding.

kind.description: The provider's name for it, such as `session` or `weekly_all`.

percent.description: 0 to 100 as the provider reported it. Not rounded, not derived.

resetsAtMs.description: Epoch ms, or null when the provider sent no reset time.

scope.description: The model a scoped limit applies to, or null.

UsageProblemKind.description: Why there is no number to show. Every one of these paints nothing.

oneOf.description: The file the reading comes from is not there.
It is there and could not be read.
It is there and is not JSON.
It holds no reading.
The reading does not have the shape the host was written against.
The reading is too old to stand behind.
Every window in it has already reset.

UsageSeverity.description: The provider's own judgement of how close a limit is.

backend.description: The backend this measures, such as `claude-code`.

fetchedAtMs.description: When the agent last had these figures from its provider, epoch ms.

file.description: The file it came from, so the number is traceable.

problem.description: Set exactly when `limits` is empty and something was wrong.

spend.description: The estimated-dollars half, or null where it has not been built.

UsageSpend.description: Estimated spend, always an estimate and labelled as one.

indexMs.description: How long the last incremental pass took, in ms.

pricedAt.description: Version of the price table, such as `2026-08-10`.

session.description: The session window, aligned with the session limit's reset.

unpricedModels.description: Models seen with no entry in the price table.

UsageTokens.description: The four token classes, priced separately.

dollars.description: US dollars, estimated from the price table.

messages.description: Assistant messages the figure is a sum over.

WatchConfigRequest.description: Which file the client's editor has open, or null to release the watch.

Welcome.description: The host's answer to an accepted `hello`.

backends.description: Every backend the host can run, with the features it declares.

capabilities.description:
The capabilities the host accepted: those the client declared that
the host knows.

hostVersion.description: The host program's own version, such as "0.4.1".

from.description:
The artifact the link was clicked in, which `[[index]]` prefers to
resolve beside.

path.description: The file, or null when nothing matches.

expectedHash.description:
The hash the editor's content came from, or null for a file it knows
does not exist yet. A mismatch stops the write.

scopePath.description: The scope's base folder, recorded on the snapshot.

conflict.description: Set when the file on disk is not what the editor was based on.

error.description: Set when the write was refused for another reason.

file.description: The file after the write, or as it stands when the write was refused.

snapshotId.description: The snapshot taken first, or null when nothing was written.

unchanged.description: The bytes were already what was asked for.

WriteConflict.description: The file on disk is not what the editor was based on.

description: Generated from the floti-protocol crate by `cargo run -p floti-protocol --bin generate`. Do not edit. Each frame is a 4-byte big-endian length and one CBOR value that is a Message.
